title: SLO declaration TTL and crediting algorithm for per-endpoint/model error budgets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a defensible algorithm and operational playbook for declaring SLOs (SLIs and targets) per endpoint/model, assigning time-to-live (TTL) semantics for SLO declarations, and an automated error-budget crediting/repayment mechanism. This ticket defines: (1) canonical SLI metrics for text generation and chat endpoints (latency, availability, quality/regression signals), (2) TTL and versioning semantics for SLO documents so that stale declarations auto-expire, (3) how error budget credits are computed and applied after incident mitigation or quality regressions, and (4) integration points with circuit breaker thresholds, multi-region failover decisions, and load-shedding priority weights.
rationale: Several incidents showed inconsistent SLO metadata and long-lived stale declarations that caused teams to make incorrect failover decisions. We need explicit TTLs so ops tooling can evict or require re-approval for old SLOs, and an algorithm to credit error budgets after compensating actions (rollbacks, model patch, capacity increases). This will enable safer automated failovers and predictable graceful degradation across regions.
sli_examples: - Latency SLI: p95 tail latency on user-facing route measured at request completion (exclude retries). - Availability SLI: success rate of 2xx/3xx responses excluding known client errors and upstream model timeouts. - Quality SLI: classification/regression score derived from a sampled promptset (daily aggregated) — distinct for deterministic and sampling models. - Cost-aware SLI: tokens-per-second per model variant for batching-sensitive routes (used by optimize to propose quantization).
slo_ttl_spec: - Default TTL: 90 days for non-enterprise routes. - Short-lived experimental SLOs: 14 days (label: experimental). - Enterprise/contracted SLOs: 365 days unless renewed. - TTL enforcement: Redwood Console will surface expiring SLOs 14 days prior and block automated rollouts when TTL expired. Expired SLOs enter 'stale' status and require explicit re-approval by PM + SRE.
error_budget_crediting_algorithm: 1) Compute baseline error budget = (1 - SLO_target) * measurement_window_tokens. 2) When an incident is classified and remediated, calculate impact_tokens = sum(tokens_in_failed_requests) during incident window. 3) Credited_tokens = min(impact_tokens, baseline_error_budget * credit_cap) where credit_cap defaults to 0.5 (50% of baseline). 4) If mitigation included a guarantee (rollback + fix within 24h), apply a bonus multiplier 1.2 up to a secondary cap. 5) Auto-apply credited_tokens to the lease for that endpoint/model and record a ledger entry. Manual disputes create a CID ticket and audit trail. 6) For quality regressions detected via evals, apply credits only after regression repro and a fix validation run passes in staging.
circuit_breaker_integration: - CB trip threshold uses burn-rate semantics: trip when (error_budget_burn_rate_over_5m > 4) AND absolute_error_rate > threshold. - When CB trips, routes with explicit high-availability tags are degraded last. - CB resets follow an exponential backoff with allowed retries tied to remaining error budget. - All CB events emit traces to tracing and an incident stub that links into the error-budget ledger.
multiregion_failover_guidance: - Prefer regional remediation for soft failures; global failover only allowed when regional error budget < critical_band (10% remaining) OR SLI shows consistent cross-region regression. - During failover, preserve model-version affinity for a tenant when possible; if a pinned variant is unavailable, fall back to nearest compatible quantized variant. - Traffic migration uses staged weights (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 5-minute observation windows and SLI checks at each stage. - Automated failover is gated by error-budget credit balance and a cooldown since last failover (default 1h).
load_shedding_priority_scheme: - Each route has a 3-tuple priority: {business_priority, degrade_grace, quality_tolerance}. - Business_priority determines eviction order (0 highest rescue -> 10 lowest). - Degrade_grace controls how long a route is allowed to run degraded before eviction. - Quality_tolerance maps to allowed quantization or cheaper variant fallbacks. - The shedding controller uses a weighted knapsack solver that optimizes for preserved revenue and SLO satisfaction across tenants.
operational_runbook: Steps for on-call when an endpoint is burning error budget: 1) Pager triggers: open incident channel and annotate with SLO key and current ledger entry. 2) Inspect SLI dashboards (latency p50/p95/p99, success rate, recent regression evals) and rollback history. 3) If CB tripped, follow CB playbook: backoff, circuit isolation, selective rate limiting. 4) If capacity saturated, enact shedding policy based on priority matrix and follow staged failover plan. 5) After remediation, create a ledger entry for credited_tokens and file a postmortem template. 6) If SLO TTL expired, tag incident as policy-violation and escalate to PM + SRE for re-declaration.
acceptance_criteria: - SLO TTLs appear in Console UI with 14-day warning and auto-stale enforcement. - Error-budget ledger entries created automatically after incident remediation or manual adjudication. - Circuit breaker events include SLO key and burn-rate evaluation in traces. - Multi-region staged failover uses the new staged-weight policy and respects cooldowns in simulated chaos test. - Unit and e2e tests for crediting algorithm with mocked incidents and quality regression harness.
